nnis.head: 35a6707b5005cbe1b718bddfba247fe41070c083
changes: stdin is capped at 1 MiB before UTF-8 decoding, JSON parsing, canonicalisation, hashing, model loading or CUDA work
text fields are capped at 1024 bytes and model/evaluation/retained collections are bounded against the exact checkpoint position capacity
the caller contract requires an independent wall deadline, bounded concurrent stdout/stderr drains and whole-process-group termination
nnis.limitation: The Tiny Llama reference workflow passed on the exact PR head and did not trigger on the target push; only target CI 759 is claimed as post-merge validation.

review_followup.finding: P1 buffered pipe close could block behind a live drain thread when an escaped descendant inherited the pipe

kvlab.head: ff8b975ddc0700c8069ace1be63e5af7c7713cda
changes: one unbuffered nonblocking selectors loop owns stdin, stdout and stderr descriptors
wall execution deadline and independent post-exit/post-kill drain deadline are enforced
stdout is retained up to 1 MiB and stderr up to 64 KiB while both pipes are drained concurrently
the original process group is killed on timeout and when inherited pipes outlive an exited leader
escaped-session descendants cannot block caller cleanup; the call fails closed without claiming the escaped process was killed
large stdin writes use persistent memoryview slices to avoid quadratic remainder copies
regressions: escaped-session descendant retaining pipes cannot extend the caller deadline
exited leader with a same-group child retaining pipes causes bounded failure and group termination
256 KiB request is sent through multiple zero-copy memoryview slices

review_followups.finding: partial writes copied the unsent payload remainder
same-group child could retain pipes after leader exit without group termination

acceptance: all size and collection bounds are applied before expensive parse/allocation/model work
caller supervision is independently deadline-bounded, drains both output streams under retention caps, and terminates the owned process group
all three integrated trees equal their exact tested head trees
NNIS target CI and the final KVLab target CI completed successfully
limitations: No network service exposure or exploitability is asserted.
An escaped descendant in a different session cannot be killed through the original group; the caller instead closes its descriptors and fails within the bounded drain deadline.
KVLab evidence is experimental/protocol qualification and is not represented as hardware performance qualification.
